intent: Test whether a wider 5-sensor spread (±0.036 m) and a narrower, larger-wheeled, lighter drivetrain (track 0.10 m, radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg) reduce line loss and off-track exits. Changes are compared with the iteration 0 baseline: spread 0.048 to 0.072 m, track 0.12 to 0.10 m, radius 0.03 to 0.035 m, mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg. The Integrator should check whether the controller can use the extra spread without oscillating.
learning: Hypotheses to test, one at a time where possible: (1) Wider spread (±0.036 m) reduces line_loss_events and max_error on the s-bend and slalom versus baseline. (2) Track 0.10 m increases turn authority, which should reduce max_error on tight bends but may raise steering_oscillation. (3) Radius 0.035 m with mass 0.6 kg raises average speed, so progress per second should rise on the oval. (4) If max_error stays near 0.06 m with few line losses, the limit is controller lag, not sensing, and the next step is a forward sensor offset change (e.g. y 0.06 m) rather than more spread. If line losses remain high, the next step is a wider spread (±0.05 m) or a larger sensor footprint (0.016 m).
rationale: The baseline reached the off-track limit (0.06 m) on every development track. Max error averaged about 0.06 m, and line-loss events averaged 1.0 to 1.35 per run. The sensor footprints are 12 mm, so the outer sensors stop seeing tape once the line moves about 0.042 m off centre (0.024 spread + 0.0125 half-tape + 0.006 half-footprint). Beyond that the controller is blind, which matches the line losses. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). With body_width at most 0.18 that gives at most 0.0575, so the limit stays at 0.06 m whatever body width I choose. Body width therefore does not help, and I leave it at 0.12. Changes for this iteration: (1) widen the sensor spread to ±0.036 m (5 sensors, 18 mm pitch). This keeps tape visible to about 0.054 m offset, which should cut line-loss events and keep the robot on the line through bends. (2) Reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. For the same wheel-speed difference, turn rate rises by about 20 percent, so the robot can follow tighter bends. (3) Raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m, which increases ground speed per unit of wheel rotation, to help the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. (4) Lower mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg to reduce inertia in bends. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, a lower max_error on s-bend and slalom, and a higher progress on oval. Finishing on the s-bend and slalom is still unlikely until the integrator tunes the controller.
